DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Hypertrophic Pyloric Stenosis (HPS)

The clinical picture of an 8-month-old male with non-bilious feeding difficulties, abdominal distension, and a history of being born at term is atypical for classic HPS, which usually presents earlier (4–8 weeks) with projectile non-bilious vomiting. Given the age and the lack of bilious vomiting, we must consider other causes of gastric outlet obstruction or functional issues. Please confirm if the baby has passed any stool in the last 24 hours and describe the consistency. I am also requesting the ultrasound results to evaluate for pyloric thickening or alternative causes like malrotation with volvulus.
